thumb.title: Who can break Pant's Rs 27 crore record?

concept: The page's auction series moves from trades to money. The hero sets the record against the purses: 'The record is Rs 27 crore.' in muted grey and 'Six teams have the money to beat it.' in white, with the total left (Rs 297.95 crore) and the 66 open spots as proof. Slide 2 is the full ten-bar purse chart, LSG's highlighted Rs 47.45 crore bar towering over GT's Rs 8.75 crore, with spots to fill under each team so fans can see money per spot, not just money. Slide 3 is one giant 'Rs 18 cr', the overseas pay cap that means a record-breaking bid lands very differently for a foreign star. The last slide pulls out what it means and asks who crosses Rs 27 crore. Business gold, type and charts only: no player photos, no team logos.
caption:
Rs 27 crore is the IPL auction record. Six teams can beat it.

Rishabh Pant went to LSG for Rs 27 crore at the 2025 auction. For the mini-auction in Goa on December 16 the ten teams have Rs 297.95 crore left between them and 66 squad spots to fill.

LSG have the most at Rs 47.45 crore, then KKR (41.65), SRH (40.15), DC (39.50), MI (32.60) and CSK (28.05). RR have Rs 27.05 crore, just 5 lakh over the record, with six spots to fill. GT have the least at Rs 8.75 crore.

The catch: at a mini-auction an overseas player is paid at most Rs 18 crore and anything bid above that goes to the BCCI. KKR bid Rs 25.20 crore for Cameron Green but he is paid Rs 18 crore. An Indian player keeps the full bid.
